title: Global Scholars Scholarship

deadline_note: Application deadlines for fall 2025 admission: Early Action/Early Decision first-year applicants 1 November; Regular Decision first-year applicants 15 January; first-year applicants for spring 2025 admission 1 November; transfer applicants for fall 2025 admission rolling 1 March to 1 May; transfer applicants for spring 2025 admission 1 November. Merit scholarship decisions are made solely on the information presented in the admission application, without consideration of financial need

verification.notes: The existence of the Global Scholars Scholarship, its place among the five merit scholarships for international first-year students, the separate essay requirement, the application deadlines and the financial aid form required were all read directly from Clark University's official financial aid and international student pages. No reachable Clark page publishes a dollar figure for the Global Scholars Scholarship itself, so funding_amount is recorded as null rather than estimated; the Presidential Scholarship figures on the Clark scholarships page describe that separate award, not this one. Note that the page at clarku.edu/financial-aid/prospective-students/international-students still describes applying by the Nov. 1 early action deadline and Jan. 15 regular decision deadline for fall 2025 admission, so the dates should be re-checked for your entry year. The second page URL listed resolves to the generic financial aid landing page.

applicant_utility: Unlike Clark's International Traina, International Achievement and International Jonas Clark Scholarships, which every international first-year applicant is considered for automatically, the Global Scholars Scholarship requires you to write a separate essay - so it is one of the few Clark awards where your own writing can move the needle rather than your transcript alone. Make sure that essay is submitted with your application and not bolted on afterwards. The application is the same one you use for admission, so there is no second deadline to track, but do complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form on your Applicant Status Portal, because Clark requires it from all international students. One caveat before you build plans around this award: Clark does not publish a dollar value for the Global Scholars Scholarship on any page you can reach, so treat the amount as unknown and check with the Office of Financial Assistance directly at finaid@clarku.edu. It is worth knowing what sits alongside it - Clark's separate Presidential Scholarship, awarded to about five students a year after finalist interviews, covers full tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for all four years - and that Clark states plainly that it is not able to offer financial assistance to cover the full cost of attendance, and that its admissions process is need-aware.

title: MSU International Student Scholarships
deadline_central_display: Nov. 1 early action deadline guarantees a decision by Jan. 15; Non-resident Scholarship decisions are released by mid-February
deadline_note: The scholarship application route for these awards is the application for admission, with no additional application needed for the Non-resident Scholarship. Applying by the Nov. 1 early action deadline guarantees a decision by January 15, and decisions for the MSU Non-resident Scholarship are released by mid-February.
application_cycle: Annual, alongside the fall and spring admission cycles
status_note: The international student scholarships page states that the application for admission is all that is needed to be considered for these awards, with decisions released by mid-February.
benefits: MSU Non-resident Scholarship award levels: President's Award $18,000, Provost's Award $15,000, Dean's Award $12,000, 1855 Scholarship $9,000, Beaumont Tower Scholarship $5,000 and Global Community Scholars Scholarship $3,000
Honors College Excellence Scholarship awards $13,000 annually over eight semesters
Professorial Assistantship offers an annual stipend of approximately $3,500 for working 8 to 10 hours per week on faculty-mentored research or scholarly activity, renewable for four semesters
Red Cedar Scholarship: $1,250 annually, renewable for eight semesters
Presidential Study Abroad Scholarship: $3,000 or $5,000 depending on the length of the programme
eligibility: Incoming first-year students with non-U.S. residency status

All international students admitted to MSU are automatically considered for the MSU Non-resident Scholarship, whose award levels are granted to high-achieving students based on their academic performance with consideration given to the overall rigour and success within their curriculum
Honors College awards require being an incoming first-year student who has been invited to the Honors College
Red Cedar Scholarship is for dependents or grandchildren of Michigan State University alumni
Honors College Distinction Scholarship is for non-resident Honors College invitees who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, or citizens of Canada or Mexico
requirements: The application for admission is all that you need to submit in order to be considered for each award unless otherwise noted
Enrol at MSU for the semester that the scholarship is awarded; the award may not be deferred to a subsequent semester of initial enrolment
Awards are limited to eight consecutive semesters of enrolment (fall and spring of an academic year) as an undergraduate
Enrol for and complete a minimum of 12 credit hours each semester
Remain in good academic standing with the university for the award to continue to disburse
Maintain international residency for tuition purposes - any change in residency status or the receipt of an international tuition waiver will impact future eligibility
Notify the Office of Financial Aid at es.scholarships@msu.edu if enrolment at MSU is disrupted and request an official leave of absence

Students receiving full or partial tuition sponsorship from their government, or a private sponsoring agency, should notify their admissions counselor, as MSU reserves the right to adjust the award in consideration of other MSU scholarships or tuition support
application_method: Submit the application for admission to MSU - consideration for the Non-resident Scholarship is automatic and no separate application is required
application_route: Apply for admission to MSU; consideration for these scholarships is automatic without a separate application, with decisions for the MSU Non-resident Scholarship released by mid-February.
study_mode: Full-time undergraduate study, minimum 12 credit hours each semester
duration: Renewable for up to eight consecutive fall and spring semesters as an undergraduate, subject to continued eligibility
description: Michigan State University awards scholarships to incoming first-year students with non-U.S. residency status, including the tiered MSU Non-resident Scholarship, Honors College scholarships, the Red Cedar Scholarship and the Presidential Study Abroad Scholarship, with the application for admission as all that is needed to be considered.

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage (MSU's international scholarship page does not state that these awards are applied specifically to tuition, so it is recorded as null)
verification.notes: All scholarship names and award amounts, the eligibility rules, the automatic-consideration statement, the limited-numbers caveat and the renewal regulations were read directly from Michigan State University's international student scholarships page and its international scholarship regulations page. All specific scholarship award amounts are listed in U.S. dollars. Two warnings appear prominently on MSU's own page: 'Only a limited number of students who are considered will receive offers for any of the following scholarships' and 'Meeting the criteria for an award does not guarantee that an offer will be made', so these should be treated as competitive rather than guaranteed. Award amounts have increased from those in the catalogue - the President's Award is now $18,000, the Provost's Award $15,000, the Dean's Award $12,000 and the 1855 Scholarship $9,000 - so a figure quoted from an older year should be checked against the current page. The Honours College Distinction Scholarship is not available to international students generally, as it is limited to non-resident invitees who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, or citizens of Canada or Mexico.

applicant_utility: The convenient thing about MSU's international scholarships is that there is no separate application: your admission application is the whole process, and all international students admitted to MSU are automatically considered for the Non-resident Scholarship. Decisions are released by mid-February, and applying by the November 1 early action deadline guarantees a decision by January 15, so early action is genuinely worth it here rather than just a marketing line. The money is tiered by achievement - President's Award $18,000, Provost's Award $15,000, Dean's Award $12,000, 1855 Scholarship $9,000, Beaumont Tower $5,000 and Global Community Scholars $3,000 - which means your award level is really a measure of your academic record and the rigour of your curriculum. Read MSU's own caveat carefully: only a limited number of considered students receive offers and meeting the criteria does not guarantee one, so have a backup plan for the gap. Renewal is not automatic. You must maintain international residency for tuition purposes, enrol for at least 12 credit hours each semester, stay in good academic standing, and tell the Office of Financial Aid if your enrolment is interrupted, including requesting an official leave of absence. If your government or a sponsoring agency is paying your tuition, notify your admissions counselor, because MSU can reduce or adjust the award in light of that support.
